records.name: Ayr Beach
records.description: Long sandy beach and esplanade popular for family walks, sea views and easy access to the town centre.

records.name: Ayr Racecourse
records.description: Ayr Racecourse at Whitletts Road, Ayr, Scotland, was opened in 1907. There are courses for flat and for National Hunt racing.
records.hours: Race days only (check ayr-racecourse.co.uk for fixtures)

records.name: Ayr Harbour
records.description: Working and leisure harbour on the River Ayr, linked to the town's maritime trade and seaside character.

records.name: Low Green
records.description: Broad seafront green space beside the beach, used for strolling, events and classic Ayr sunsets.

records.name: Auld Kirk of Ayr
records.description: Auld Kirk of Ayr is a 17th-century Category A listed church in Ayr. The church sits on the site of an earlier monastery.

records.name: Loudoun Hall
records.description: One of Ayr's oldest surviving houses, a turreted burgh building linked with civic life and centuries of High Street history.

records.name: Ayr Town Hall
records.description: Ayr Town Hall is a municipal building in New Bridge Street, Ayr, Scotland. The town hall, which was the headquarters of Ayr Burgh Council, is a Category A listed building.

records.name: Ayr Carnegie Library
records.description: Historic Carnegie library building reflecting the civic ambition of Victorian Ayr and the town's cultural heritage.

records.name: Tam o' Shanter Experience
records.description: Burns-themed heritage attraction in Ayr celebrating Tam o' Shanter and the town's literary connection with Robert Burns.

records.name: Belleisle Park
records.description: Large public park around Belleisle House with formal gardens, woodland walks, golf and wide views toward the Doon valley.

records.name: Rozelle Park
records.description: Landscaped south Ayr park with gardens, sculpture trails and easy access to the town's Burns Country attractions.

records.name: Rozelle House
records.description: Victorian mansion within Rozelle Park that now hosts art exhibitions and local cultural displays.

records.name: River Ayr Way
records.description: The River Ayr Way is a long-distance path in Ayrshire, Scotland. The route, which is 66 km long, follows the course of the River Ayr from its source at Glenbuck Loch to the sea at Ayr, where the trail links with the Ayrshire Coastal Path. The path was developed as part of the Coalfield Access Project, a funding package of £2.5m that was used to improve public access to the countryside in the former mining districts of Ayrshire. The route was officially opened in 2006 by broadcaster Fred Macaulay, and is now designated as one of Scotland's Great Trails by NatureScot. As of 2018 about 137,000 people were using the path each year, of whom about 41,000 walked the entire route.

records.name: Greenan Castle
records.description: Greenan Castle is a 16th-century ruined tower house, around 2+1⁄2 miles southwest of Ayr in South Ayrshire, Scotland. Situated at the top of a sea cliff, it was originally a promontory fort converted into a motte-and-bailey in the 12th century. In the 15th century a tower house was built by the Lords of the Isles, which later passed into the hands of the Kennedy family.

records.name: Electric Brae
records.description: The Electric Brae is a gravity hill in South Ayrshire, Scotland, where a freewheeling vehicle will appear to be drawn uphill by some mysterious attraction. The phenomenon is an optical illusion.

records.name: Wellington Square
records.description: Elegant Georgian square near the seafront, lined with handsome terraces and long associated with civic Ayr.

records.name: Burns Monument Centre
records.description: Restored church building used for exhibitions and events, and one of Ayr's most distinctive civic spaces.

records.name: Heads of Ayr Farm Park
records.description: Popular family attraction on the coast with outdoor play areas, animal encounters and sea views toward Arran.

records.name: Craigie House
records.description: Historic house and estate long associated with the Craigie district and the wider story of Ayr's southern edge.

records.name: Auld Brig
records.description: Famous old bridge over the River Ayr celebrated in Burns's poem The Brigs of Ayr and central to the town's story.

records.name: Wallace Tower
records.description: Small surviving civic tower and landmark recalling older municipal Ayr and its market traditions.

records.name: Ayr Citadel
records.description: Historic defensive quarter linked with Cromwell's citadel and later military use near the river mouth.

records.name: Belleisle House
records.description: Grand house within Belleisle Park, lending architectural interest to one of Ayr's finest green spaces.

records.name: Belleisle Conservatory
records.description: Glasshouse and formal garden area within Belleisle Park, adding a classic Victorian park flourish.

records.name: Rozelle Estate Trails
records.description: Wooded and landscaped footpaths around the Rozelle estate, ideal for gentle walks close to Alloway.

records.name: Ayr Pavilion
records.description: Longstanding seafront entertainment venue marking Ayr's development as a popular Clyde coast resort.

records.name: Lang Scots Mile
records.description: Classic local stroll along the seafront, prized for sunsets, sea air and easy walking between beach landmarks.

records.name: Seafield Golf Course
records.description: Municipal coastal golf course south of the town, offering open views across Ayr Bay and Arran.

records.name: Burns Statue Square
records.description: Busy town-centre square named for Robert Burns and a useful stop when exploring Ayr's civic core.

records.name: St John's Tower
records.description: Surviving medieval tower fragment reflecting the age and importance of old Ayr's ecclesiastical quarter.

records.name: New Bridge
records.description: Principal crossing over the River Ayr that frames good views back toward the harbour and old town bridges.

records.name: Ayr Mercat Cross
records.description: Symbolic market-cross location evoking Ayr's long burgh history and commercial traditions.

records.name: Ayr Esplanade
records.description: Wide promenade running beside the beach and Low Green, perfect for an easy seafront walk.

records.name: River Ayr Mouth
records.description: Pleasant waterside viewpoint where river, harbour and sea scenery meet at the edge of town.

records.name: Alloway Railway Tunnel
records.description: Atmospheric old rail corridor near Alloway, now remembered as part of the area's transport heritage.

records.name: Seafield Beach
records.description: Quieter stretch of Ayr's shoreline south of the main beach, good for long coastal walks.

records.name: Ayrshire Coastal Path - Ayr Section
records.description: Long-distance coastal trail section linking Ayr's beach, harbour, dunes and outlying shorelines.

records.name: Gaiety Theatre
records.description: Victorian theatre and arts venue contributing to Ayr's lively cultural life in the town centre.

records.name: Craigie Park
records.description: Neighbourhood green space in the Craigie district with mature trees and a quieter local feel.

records.name: Belleisle Golf Course
records.description: Well-known parkland course beside Belleisle Park, adding golfing heritage to the south Ayr landscape.
